comment: iOS App Privacy nutrition label — declare what data the app collects. It has to match what the build actually sends: constants/legal.ts, android_data_safety.json and the hosted policy at bugrout.app/privacy all describe the same list (#206). PostHog is deliberately absent: no eas.json profile sets EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY, so no shipped build initialises it. Setting that key means adding Usage Data (Product Interaction) and a second Device ID entry here and in the other three.

data_types.collection: Required for routing — the trip's start point and destination are sent to BugRout's routing service (EXPO_PUBLIC_VALHALLA_URL). Also sent with the optional Crowd Signal opt-in, rounded to 4 decimal places (~11 m), which Apple counts as precise.
The centre point or bounding box of a map region you chose to download, sent to the National Weather Service, Overpass and FEMA ESF6-SS to fetch threats and resources
Destination search text is sent to Nominatim, the OpenStreetMap Foundation's geocoder, to be turned into coordinates (#208)
Optional — the Crowd Signal opt-in sends a random token that rotates every 24 hours, so signals from one device are grouped within that window
Optional — sent via Sentry only after the Crash Reports opt-in in Settings, which is off by default
